agent.problem: The setup says the LORD has listened to the psalmist "once," suggesting a single occasion, but verse 2 gives no number of times. This unsupported detail is presented as context rather than as the part of the statement being tested.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

agent.problem: The baker is asked to complete the unseen wording of verse 5, "full of ___." Compassion, power and wisdom are all plausible things to say about God after a rescue, so this becomes a guess at the line's final word rather than a question about its movement or meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: The card simply asks the baker to supply the unseen last word of the psalmist's line to his soul by completing "return to its ___." That is wording completion rather than a meaningful question about why he speaks to his soul or what has changed.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: "His soul, his eyes AND his feet, all covered." "Friend, that’s not a rescue." "That’s the DELUXE package."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: This card only restates the three parts of verse 8 that the baker just supplied on card 13 and adds a joke. It introduces no new passage content and does not move the psalm forward toward verse 9.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

agent.problem: The question asks the baker to complete the unseen ending of verse 16, "He has broken his ___." The setup about calling himself the LORD's servant does not turn this into a question about the verse's movement or meaning; it remains a guess at the line's final word.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
